CWE-89.title: SQL Injection
CWE-89.business_impact: An attacker can read, modify, or delete arbitrary data in the backing database, potentially exposing sensitive customer or financial records and undermining data integrity.
CWE-89.remediation: Use parameterized queries or an ORM with bound parameters for all database access; never concatenate untrusted input into SQL strings. Apply least-privilege database accounts and validate/allowlist input where feasible.

stack_patterns.fastapi: In FastAPI/SQLAlchemy, always use bound ORM filters or `text('... WHERE id = :id').bindparams(id=val)` rather than f-strings inside raw SQL.
stack_patterns.django: Use Django ORM QuerySet methods (`Model.objects.filter(col=val)`) and pass `%s` params list to `cursor.execute(sql, [val])` when using raw cursors.
stack_patterns.laravel: Use Eloquent bindings or `DB::select('SELECT ... WHERE id = ?', [$id])` and avoid unescaped `DB::raw()` interpolation.
stack_patterns.express: Use prepared placeholders (`$1` in pg / `?` in mysql2) or parameterized Prisma/Knex builders instead of template literal SQL.
stack_patterns.spring_boot: Use Spring Data JPA derived queries or `@Query` named parameters (`:param`) / `JdbcTemplate` bind arguments.
stack_patterns.gin: Use `db.QueryContext(ctx, 'SELECT ... WHERE id = $1', id)` or GORM struct/placeholder conditions instead of `fmt.Sprintf`.
stack_patterns.python: Pass parameters as a tuple/dict second argument to DB-API `cursor.execute(query, params)` and never format SQL strings.

CWE-79.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
CWE-79.business_impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary script in a victim's browser session, enabling session hijacking, credential theft, or defacement of the application.
CWE-79.remediation: Contextually encode/escape all untrusted output rendered in HTML, JS, or URL contexts. Apply a strict Content-Security-Policy and use templating engines with automatic output escaping enabled.

stack_patterns.fastapi: Enable Jinja2 `select_autoescape(['html', 'xml'])` for HTML views and validate rich HTML server-side via nh3/bleach.
stack_patterns.laravel: Always output variables via Blade `{{ $var }}` instead of raw `{!! $var !!}`, and pair session cookies with `HttpOnly` + CSP.
stack_patterns.express: Avoid injecting unescaped HTML into `res.send(...)`; escape HTML contexts and enforce strict CSP headers via Helmet.
stack_patterns.nextjs: Rely on React JSX auto-escaping and sanitize any `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` payload with DOMPurify.
stack_patterns.django: Keep Django template autoescaping active and avoid marking user-controlled strings with `mark_safe()`.

CWE-22.title: Path Traversal
CWE-22.business_impact: An attacker can read or write files outside the intended directory, potentially exposing configuration secrets or achieving remote code execution.
CWE-22.remediation: Resolve and canonicalize user-supplied paths, then verify they remain within an allowlisted base directory before use. Avoid passing raw user input directly to filesystem APIs.

stack_patterns.fastapi: Use `Path(base_dir, safe_name).resolve().is_relative_to(base_dir.resolve())` or map opaque UUID keys rather than client filenames.
stack_patterns.python: Canonicalize via `Path.resolve()` and assert `.is_relative_to(BASE_DIR)` before opening files.
stack_patterns.express: Use `path.resolve(BASE_DIR, name)` and verify `resolved.startsWith(BASE_DIR + path.sep)` before `fs`/`res.sendFile` calls.
stack_patterns.go: Clean input with `filepath.Base` and confirm `strings.HasPrefix(cleanPath, baseDir+string(filepath.Separator))`.

CWE-287.title: Improper Authentication
CWE-287.business_impact: An attacker can bypass identity verification entirely, gaining unauthorized access to protected functionality or data.
CWE-287.remediation: Enforce authentication on every protected endpoint via centralized middleware/guards rather than ad-hoc per-route checks. Use well-vetted authentication libraries and require strong credential/session validation.

stack_patterns.fastapi: Apply `Depends(get_current_user)` on routers/endpoints, validate JWT `alg`, `exp`, and `token_version`, and avoid fallback unsigned tokens.
stack_patterns.express: Mount authentication middleware globally at the router prefix, pin JWT algorithms explicitly, and rotate session identifiers upon login.
stack_patterns.laravel: Enforce `auth:sanctum` or `auth` middleware on route groups and validate signed tokens consistently.
stack_patterns.spring_boot: Configure Spring Security `SecurityFilterChain` with default-deny `.anyRequest().authenticated()` and permit only explicit public paths.

CWE-200.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information
CWE-200.business_impact: Sensitive internal data (configuration, credentials, PII) is disclosed to unauthorized parties, risking compliance violations and further compromise.
CWE-200.remediation: Apply strict output filtering and access controls on any endpoint or error message that could reveal internal state. Review logs, debug endpoints, and error traces for inadvertent data leakage.

CWE-538.title: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
CWE-538.business_impact: Sensitive files (e.g. VCS metadata, environment configuration) are reachable by unauthenticated clients, potentially exposing credentials or source code.
CWE-538.remediation: Exclude sensitive directories (.git, .env, backups) from the web root or explicitly deny access to them at the reverse proxy/server configuration level.

CWE-502.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.business_impact: An attacker can craft malicious serialized payloads to achieve remote code execution or denial of service when deserialized by the application.
CWE-502.remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data with formats that support arbitrary object instantiation (e.g. pickle). Prefer safe data formats (JSON) with strict schema validation.

CWE-306.title: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-306.business_impact: Exposed administrative interfaces, datastores, or critical operations can be invoked by unauthenticated actors, risking total service compromise or data exfiltration.
CWE-306.remediation: Require strong authentication on every exposed network service and administrative endpoint, and bind internal datastores (such as Redis/PostgreSQL) to private subnets only.

CWE-319.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
CWE-319.business_impact: Credentials, session cookies, or sensitive business payloads transmitted over unencrypted channels can be intercepted or modified by network eavesdroppers.
CWE-319.remediation: Enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 for all external and internal traffic, redirect HTTP to HTTPS with HSTS enabled, and mark session cookies with the Secure flag.

CWE-326.title: Inadequate Encryption Strength
CWE-326.business_impact: Deprecated TLS protocols or weak cryptographic ciphers allow attackers to downgrade connections or recover protected session traffic.
CWE-326.remediation: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, RC4, and 3DES ciphers on reverse proxies and load balancers; enforce TLS 1.2+ with AEAD cipher suites.

CWE-352.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
CWE-352.business_impact: Authenticated users can be tricked into executing unintended state-changing actions (such as password changes or fund transfers) via malicious third-party sites.
CWE-352.remediation: Protect state-changing cookie-authenticated endpoints with anti-CSRF synchronizer tokens, validate Origin/Referer headers, and configure SameSite=Lax or Strict cookies.

stack_patterns.django: Keep `CsrfViewMiddleware` enabled and never mark state-changing authenticated views with `@csrf_exempt`.
stack_patterns.laravel: Ensure `VerifyCsrfToken` covers all state-mutating routes using cookie sessions and include `@csrf` in forms.
stack_patterns.express: Bind anti-CSRF tokens for cookie-backed sessions, set `SameSite=Lax`/`Strict`, and check `Origin` headers.

CWE-639.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (IDOR/BOLA)
CWE-639.business_impact: Authenticated attackers can manipulate object identifiers to read or alter records belonging to other tenants or users, causing severe privacy and compliance breaches.
CWE-639.remediation: Verify tenant and object ownership server-side on every request using the authenticated user's session context rather than trusting client-supplied IDs.

stack_patterns.fastapi: Scope every SQLAlchemy query with `.filter_by(id=resource_id, workspace_id=current_workspace.id)` rather than `db.get(Model, resource_id)` alone.
stack_patterns.django: Filter querysets by tenant/owner (`Model.objects.filter(id=pk, workspace=request.workspace)`) inside views and ViewSets.
stack_patterns.laravel: Register Laravel Policies and scope Eloquent route bindings to the authenticated tenant/workspace.
stack_patterns.spring_boot: Enforce `@PreAuthorize` ownership checks and tenant-scoped repository predicates on every resource lookup.

CWE-693.title: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-693.business_impact: Missing or misconfigured security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) weaken browser-side defenses against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and XSS.
CWE-693.remediation: Configure strict Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY across all HTTP responses.

stack_patterns.fastapi: Attach a FastAPI middleware or reverse-proxy rules injecting CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response.
stack_patterns.express: Enable Helmet (`app.use(helmet())`) with strict explicit CSP directives and disable `X-Powered-By`.

CWE-798.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-798.business_impact: Embedded API keys, database passwords, or signing secrets allow attackers with source or artifact access to compromise backend infrastructure directly.
CWE-798.remediation: Remove all hard-coded secrets from source code and configuration files, rotate exposed credentials immediately, and inject secrets at runtime via environment/vault managers.

CWE-918.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
CWE-918.business_impact: An attacker can coerce the server into probing internal services, localhost ports, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254) to steal IAM credentials.
CWE-918.remediation: Resolve target DNS once, reject loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT IPs, restrict URI schemes to https, disable redirects, and connect directly to the validated IP.

stack_patterns.fastapi: Validate resolved `ipaddress` values (`is_private`, `is_loopback`, `is_link_local`) before calling `httpx` with `follow_redirects=False`.
stack_patterns.python: Resolve hostnames via `socket.getaddrinfo`, reject reserved/private CIDRs, disable HTTP redirects, and pin connection timeouts.
stack_patterns.go: Implement a custom `net.Dialer.Control` callback verifying resolved IPs are public unicast before opening TCP sockets.

UNKNOWN.title: Unclassified Vulnerability
UNKNOWN.business_impact: This finding could not be matched to a known CWE category. Its business impact should be assessed manually based on the specific vulnerability details before this report is finalized.
UNKNOWN.remediation: Review the finding's evidence and CVSS vector manually, consult the relevant CWE taxonomy entry if one becomes available, and apply remediation guidance specific to the underlying weakness class.
